title: Time to Cash in Your U.S. Savings Bonds?
author: Unknown
content: No U.S. savings bonds can be transferred, sold, or traded to another party. You can cash in most paper bonds (with some exceptions) at your bank or credit union. You can cash in electronic bonds online with TreasuryDirect, which will send the cash from the bond to your savings or checking account within two business days. There are some bonds that you cannot cash at your bank, including HH Series Savings Bonds. To cash in your EE Savings Bonds, you only have to log into TreasuryDirect and follow their directions. If you are cashing a full or partial amount, it can be sent from TreasuryDirect to your checking or savings account. If you have paper bonds, you can just ask your bank or credit union. Avoiding taxes when you cash out your bonds, depends on a few criteria. For example, Series I Bonds can be used (tax-free) to pay for education costs. Series I Bonds are subject to federal taxes but not state and local taxes. When you purchase Series EE or Series I Bonds you can pay taxes on the interest each year, or you can pay it at the end of its term. Overall, if you cash out bonds, you must pay tax on the interest the bond earns, unless it is used for education or under specific conditions.
